environment.machine: Apple silicon Mac, quiet local machine
environment.php: 8.5.4 (bench recording; the core and bundle suites also pass on 8.2.33)
environment.note: The record is regenerated by hand on a clean local machine with the --baseline-out flag of each timing tool; concurrent modes record the conservative of two consecutive runs. Asset rows: the eager widget driver, the worker/runtime glue, the lazy widget modules and the execution interpreter are fingerprinted at their shipped bytes; compressed sizes use gzip -n -9 and brotli -q 11, perf-budget.sh verifies the recorded raw_bytes byte-for-byte, and the compressed bytes are equality-gated per zlib encoder family. Response-shape rows: the deterministic largest-wire probe of perf-budget.sh measures the wire shapes; the execution-armed row is measured at the manifest execution-version maximum and the maximum valid execution-program op count, with the RSW fixture row included. Structured fields are authoritative; prose records how the record is made, never a second set of numbers. Historical narration belongs in the changelog; the structured fields are the single authority.

widget_driver.note: The eager driver core (widget-driver.js), three byte-identical copies, the always-loaded asset; the lazy widget modules (widget-risk.js / widget-telemetry.js / widget-locales.js / widget-compat.js) and the execution interpreter carry their own budget rows. The raw cap is carried onto the always-loaded core; the compressed caps are the ordinary-bootstrap target. Compressed sizes use gzip -n -9 and brotli -q 11. perf-budget.sh verifies the recorded raw_bytes equals the current measured bytes. Structured fields are authoritative.

headroom_review.gzip: reviewed 2026-10-06: 30802/32000 bytes (96.3%). The Object.create(null) prototype-pollution hardening of the dictionary maps raised the eager driver core on purpose; the gzip cap is re-baselined to 32,000 to cover that hardening. The eager driver core still carries the always-loaded bootstrap (solvers, lifecycle, a11y, provider surface). The reviewed follow-up stands: move the pure-JS SHA-256 fallback (the largest non-bootstrap block, only reached when neither wasm nor the worker is available) into a lazy module before the next behavior wave. Any further growth must either recover bytes or re-review this note.

widget_worker.note: The worker asset (kiwi-worker.js), three byte-identical copies; since the r8 glue-embedding change the asset is assembled by tools/embed-worker as the `var window = self;` prelude plus the full wasm glue (kiwicaptcha-wasm.js) plus the worker solver source, so a files-mode worker boots with wasm in scope (SHA solves in the worker use solve_sha256_chunk; the rsw sequential time-lock solver stays pure JS BigInt, exactly the Argon worker's loading and message pattern). The lazy runtime fetch of the driver stays for the compat tier. The row carries no cap fields by design, like the widget_runtime and widget_css rows: the asset is lazy in the files tier (a SHA-only page never fetches it) and perf-budget.sh verifies the recorded raw_bytes equals the current measured bytes.

widget_runtime.note: The wasm glue runtime asset (kiwicaptcha-wasm.js), three byte-identical copies; the embedded worker source is regenerated from the worker solver source (the tail of assets/kiwi-worker.js) by the embed-worker tool, so the rsw solver rides the glue copy too; the release worker asset embeds this same glue text, so the files-mode worker needs no runtime fetch to solve. perf-budget.sh verifies the recorded raw_bytes equals the current measured bytes.

widget_css.note: The widget stylesheet (widget.css), three byte-identical copies; perf-budget.sh verifies the recorded raw_bytes equals the current measured bytes. Structured fields are authoritative. The narrow-container wrapping fix (status text wraps instead of ellipsizing) intentionally grew the sheet; the row carries no cap by design.

widget_execution.note: The execution interpreter asset, the lazy module the armed execution dimension fetches. Compressed sizes use gzip -n -9 and brotli -q 11. Structured raw/gzip/brotli fields and the hard caps are authoritative. The version-6 real-platform rung raised the record and all three caps deliberately (the five platform probes and the async runner): 49,353 raw / 14,592 gzip / 12,518 brotli, caps 56,000 / 16,500 / 14,000.

challenge_response_json.note: The wire shape of the bundle /challenge response, decoy armed; the grammar-composed name length varies the size between runs.

challenge_response_json_execution.note: The wire shape of the bundle /challenge response when the execution dimension is armed (the authenticated decoy rides along). Maximum deterministic execution-enabled challenge response at the manifest execution-version maximum and maximum valid execution-program op count. RSW fixture included. Re-recorded at the version-6 rung (op-count ceiling 20 + byte % 4, top 23). The per-algorithm ranges are the measured spread of the drawn program operands across hand re-measurement runs. Structured min/max, op count, version and cap fields are authoritative.

widget_risk.note: The lazy adaptive-risk module (widget-risk.js), three byte-identical copies; carries the Argon2id/rsw worker solve tier, the ExecutionChallengeV1 runner and the decoy/honeypot machinery. Compressed sizes use gzip -n -9 and brotli -q 11. Structured raw/gzip/brotli fields are authoritative (perf-budget.sh equality-gates them).

widget_telemetry.note: The lazy telemetry module (widget-telemetry.js), three byte-identical copies; mode-gated session factory, never fetched unless telemetry is enabled. Carries the telemetry-v1 aggregate session: FORM-level capture-phase listeners (a widget-only degrade without a form) and the published payload contract (event-class counts, one quantized inter-event entropy value, focus transitions, paste-versus-type ratio, sample count; protocol/telemetry-v1/payload.json). Structured raw/gzip/brotli fields are authoritative (perf-budget.sh equality-gates them).

widget_compat.note: The compatibility-loader module (widget-compat.js), three byte-identical copies. Delivered inside the /api.js loader response (glue + driver core + risk module + compat module) and never fetched elsewhere; the compat markup issues the lazy widget-locales.js URL + SRI digest as container attributes. Compressed sizes use gzip -n -9 and brotli -q 11. Structured raw/gzip/brotli fields are authoritative (perf-budget.sh equality-gates them).

headroom_review.raw: reviewed 2026-10-06: 32183/32768 bytes (98.2%). The Object.create(null) prototype-pollution hardening raised the compat loader on purpose. The compat loader is already lazy (only the /api.js route pays for it) and its code is dense with no non-bootstrap block left to extract; the reviewed follow-up is a source-level compaction pass of the loader parser and descriptor table before the next compat behavior wave.

widget_locales.note: The lazy non-default locale packs (widget-locales.js), three byte-identical copies. Loaded by the eager core only when kiwiResolveLang() resolves a non-default language; a default-language page pays zero bytes. Never embedded inline (the compat loader carries its descriptor; the Symfony theme and the fixture issue data-kiwi-locales-src/-integrity in both asset tiers). Compressed sizes use gzip -n -9 and brotli -q 11. Structured raw/gzip/brotli fields are authoritative (perf-budget.sh equality-gates them).

widget_shims.note: The standalone incumbent API shims (widget-shims.js), three byte-identical copies. Fetched only by a page that presents the provider globals (grecaptcha / hcaptcha / turnstile) over a plain driver bootstrap, or that keeps Altcha / Friendly Captcha element markup; an ordinary widget page pays zero bytes. The /api.js?compat=... loader route carries widget-compat.js instead, so the two compat surfaces never load together. Compressed sizes use gzip -n -9 and brotli -q 11. Structured raw/gzip/brotli fields are authoritative (perf-budget.sh equality-gates them).

webauthn_ceremony.note: The combined WebAuthn ceremony script (create vs get, branched on doc.ceremony), three byte-identical copies, served from the content-addressed asset route for strict-CSP deployments without per-request nonces.
